Analytic Jacobian of the AC/DC formulation Rows as in compute_f:

P (AC buses), Q, loss_vsc, Imax_vsc, droop_vsc, pdc_vsc, vmdc_diff, dI_dc, loss_hvdc, inj_hvdc, Pf_cbr, Pt_cbr, Qf_cbr, Qt_cbr

Columns as in x2var:

Va, Vm, Ifp_vsc, Pt_vsc, Qt_vsc, Pf_hvdc, Pt_hvdc, Qf_hvdc, Qt_hvdc, m, tau

Parameters:

  • nbus – number of buses

  • nbr – number of passive branches

  • nvsc – number of VSCs

  • nhvdc – number of HVDC lines

  • F – passive branch from-bus indices

  • T – passive branch to-bus indices

  • Fdcp_vsc – VSC positive pole bus indices

  • Fdcn_vsc – VSC negative pole bus indices (-1 if not there)

  • T_vsc – VSC AC bus indices

  • F_hvdc – HVDC from-bus indices

  • T_hvdc – HVDC to-bus indices

  • tap_angles – branch tap angles (expanded)

  • tap_modules – branch tap modules (expanded)

  • V – complex bus voltages

  • Vm – voltage magnitudes

  • Va – voltage angles

  • I0 – current injections vector

  • u_cbr_m – branches with unknown tap module

  • u_cbr_tau – branches with unknown tap angle

  • k_cbr_pf – branches with Pf controlled

  • k_cbr_pt – branches with Pt controlled

  • k_cbr_qf – branches with Qf controlled

  • k_cbr_qt – branches with Qt controlled

  • u_vsc_ifp – VSCs whose positive pole current is unknown

  • u_vsc_pt – VSCs whose Pt is unknown

  • u_vsc_qt – VSCs whose Qt is unknown

  • k_vsc_imax – VSCs working at maximum current

  • alpha2 – VSC linear loss coefficients

  • alpha3 – VSC quadratic loss coefficients

  • hvdc_r – HVDC resistances [pu]

  • hvdc_droop – HVDC droop gains

  • i_u_vm – buses with unknown Vm

  • i_u_va – buses with unknown Va

  • i_k_p – buses with P balance (AC only)

  • i_k_q – buses with Q balance (of course AC only)

  • Ifp_vsc – VSC positive pole currents

  • Udc_vsc – signed pole-to-return DC voltage per VSC

  • k_vsc_pfp_droop – droop-controlled VSC indices

  • droop_factor – voltage sensitivity factor per droop equation

  • k_vsc_pdc – fixed-Pdc VSC indices

  • pdc_factor – voltage sensitivity factor per Pdc equation (Ifp)

  • k_vsc_vmdc_diff – bipolar Vm_dc pole-to-pole VSC indices

  • dc_rows – non-grounded DC bus indices

  • Vdc_bus – signed DC voltage per bus (Vm * cos(Va))

  • S0r – real part of the base power injections per bus [pu]

  • Y0r – real part of the base admittance injections per bus [pu]

  • Pt_vsc – VSC AC active powers

  • Qt_vsc – VSC AC reactive powers

  • Pf_hvdc – HVDC from-side active powers

VeraGridEngine.Simulations.PowerFlow.Formulations.pf_full_acdc_with_negative_poles.calc_autodiff_jacobian(func: Callable[[ndarray[tuple[Any, ...], dtype[float64]]], ndarray[tuple[Any, ...], dtype[float64]]], x: ndarray[tuple[Any, ...], dtype[float64]], sparsity: CSC, h: float = 1e-08) → CSC[source]

Compute a sparse finite-difference Jacobian using column coloring.

Columns with disjoint residual support are perturbed together. The values remain finite differences of func; the supplied analytic matrix is used only as the structural sparsity contract.

Parameters:

  • func – function accepting a vector x and args, and returning either a vector or a tuple where the first argument is a vector and the second.

  • x – Point at which to evaluate the Jacobian (numpy array).

  • sparsity – Structural Jacobian pattern at the current formulation state.

  • h – Small step for finite difference.

Returns:

Jacobian matrix as a CSC matrix.
